claim.why_it_matters: A headword, its sub-entry and the next headword are merged on one line. The index is informative, but a flattened or merged index entry misattributes page references to the wrong headword.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page (printed 907, PDF p931) shows three separate index lines at the top of the left column: headword 'CODE-SET clause 68, 309, 387', an indented sub-entry 'File description entry 271', and a new headword 'Collating sequence 231'. page-931.md line 3 holds all three as one paragraph with no '\' line break and no ' ' indent, while every other entry on the page uses that encoding (e.g. 'COLLATING SEQUENCE clause 256\' then ' FILE-CONTROL paragraph 248\'). No words or numbers are missing, but the index hierarchy is lost: the markdown reads as a single entry, so 'Collating sequence 231' is no longer a headword and 271 is not shown as a sub-entry of CODE-SET clause. The claim quotes both sources accurately. This is an informative annex, so structural (not normative) severity is right.
